summary: Unhappy-path's own report explicitly offered a downgrade path contingent on confirming design intent against the master/delivery plan, and NOT on my own unilateral judgment: 'confirm... before treating as BLOCKING vs. reclassifying MEDIUM'. I traced this against the DELIVERY-PLAN and KICKOFF (both pre-existing, Fable-reviewed planning docs, not authored in this session) and confirmed the identity-only counting shape - explicitly rejecting a finer-grained per-rule/per-episode retry-credit ledger as 'more invasive than the Application struct' - was the deliberate, reviewed decision-1 design, not an oversight. This does NOT violate the core K-eligibility safety invariant (a waived receipt is, at the moment of waiver, still genuinely Wedged and still its key's FIFO-front claim) - it affects only how many of the operator's own retries a freshly-wedged rule is guaranteed. Recording this as I7 (a documentation gap for a shipped behavioral nuance, since this consequence was not previously spelled out anywhere) rather than a correctness defect (I1-I5), and NOT applying an E6 dormancy cap myself despite the mechanism being unreachable in any shipped build today (independently confirmed by enterprise-readiness at Gate 6) - that specific severity move would weaken the band and, per the ledger's own de-escalation rule, requires an adjudicated_by who is not this change's author. None was obtained in this run (Gate 5/6 reviewers were shown my own 'already closed' framing of this finding in their prompts, which makes their agreement an ECHO, not an independent confirmation, per the ledger's own counting rule). Fixed at the honestly-derived SHOULD level: added an explicit paragraph to the design doc's R5.3 Mechanism section spelling out the consequence and citing the delivery plan's own rejection of the alternative, plus a new regression test pinning the behavior as deliberate and exercised (a mutation reintroducing wedge-type gating on reapply_count would now fail this test).
